title: Jack and the Little Tire Roads
synopsis: Jack makes tracks with two toy wheels and discovers why the grooves in real vehicle tires are useful on wet roads.
continuity_state: Before: Aunt Jo's yellow work van has been repaired and returned to service. Ms. Pam operates the Red Door Garage and the children have met the flatbed, gauge and lift. After: Jack adds two different toy-wheel patterns and a drawing of tire grooves to his blue notebook. Ms. Pam's clean demonstration toy wheels stay at the garage; the van, park and farm are unchanged.

rationale_citations.story_anchor: The grooves in many road tires help water move away from where the tire touches the road.
rationale_citations.editorial_rationale: Tread grooves channel water away from the contact patch during wet driving, supporting traction.
